chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Taxonomy of Alternative Data

lessons.title: Satellite Imagery and Geolocation Data for Economic Signals

body.text: A satellite does not care about your quarter end. It photographs a cement plant's stockyard, a port's berths, and a farmer's field on the same schedule every single day, whether or not a company feels like disclosing what is happening down there.

children.text: Satellite and geolocation data is the category most people associate with 'alternative data' first, thanks to the famous story of hedge funds counting cars in retailer parking lots. This lesson goes past that one example into the three data types you will actually work with, why India's monsoon makes one of them non-negotiable, and where these sources genuinely help versus where they are overhyped.
Three Data Types Under One Umbrella

body.caption: Optical imagery, radar imagery, and geolocation panels solve different problems

cells: Visible-light images of plants, stockpiles, ports, construction sites, and vehicles
High resolution and intuitive to interpret, but blocked by cloud cover
Surface reflectivity captured using radar wavelengths instead of visible light
Sees through cloud cover and works at night, at the cost of being harder to interpret visually
Aggregated, anonymized counts of mobile devices present at a location over time
Directly measures human footfall rather than inferring it from a photograph

children.text: Why SAR Matters More in India Than in Most Markets

markDefs.definition: Synthetic Aperture Radar. A satellite imaging technique that sends radar pulses toward the earth's surface and measures the reflected signal, producing usable images through cloud cover and darkness, unlike ordinary optical cameras.

children.text: India's monsoon runs roughly from June to September, and for a large part of that stretch, thick cloud cover makes optical satellite imagery over much of the country unusable for weeks at a time. This is exactly the four-month window when you most want visibility into crop growth, reservoir levels, and construction progress.
imagery keeps working straight through the cloud cover, which is why any India-focused monitoring program that only licenses optical imagery has a built-in blind spot for a third of the year.

body.label: India's monsoon window
body.context: The four months when optical satellite coverage is least reliable over much of India, and when SAR's ability to see through clouds matters most for continuous monitoring.

markDefs.definition: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index. A measure of plant health derived from how much near-infrared versus red light a surface reflects. Healthy, dense vegetation reflects far more near-infrared light than red light, giving it a high NDVI value.

children.text: Open satellite programs such as ESA's Sentinel missions and NASA's Landsat and MODIS provide free, publicly available imagery that can be turned into

, a running read on crop health across a state or district, weeks ahead of any official agricultural ministry estimate. In an economy where monsoon strength still drives rural income, this matters well beyond agri-commodity trading. Rural demand shows up directly in tractor makers like Mahindra & Mahindra and Escorts Kubota, two-wheeler volumes for Hero MotoCorp, and the rural revenue mix of large FMCG companies, so a below-normal NDVI reading in a key agricultural belt is a signal worth watching across several sectors at once, not just for agri-commodity desks.

body.caption: NIR is near-infrared reflectance, Red is red-band reflectance. Values range from -1 to 1: healthy dense vegetation typically scores 0.6 to 0.9, bare soil scores low positive values, and water scores negative.

body.title: Calculate NDVI for a Field
body.prompt: A satellite pixel over a wheat field records a near-infrared reflectance of 0.50 and a red reflectance of 0.10. Using NDVI = (NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red), what is the NDVI value, rounded to two decimal places?
body.explanation: NDVI = (0.50 - 0.10) / (0.50 + 0.10) = 0.40 / 0.60 = 0.667, which rounds to 0.67. This sits comfortably in the range associated with healthy, dense vegetation, well above the low values you would see over bare soil or a stressed, sparse crop.

children.text: Tracking Trade Flows With Ship Positions: AIS Data

markDefs.definition: Automatic Identification System. A maritime safety technology requiring large commercial vessels to continuously broadcast their identity, position, speed, and heading. This broadcast is picked up by satellites and shore stations and aggregated by commercial vendors into trackable shipping data.

children.text: Large commercial vessels are required, under international maritime safety rules, to continuously broadcast their position through

. Vendors aggregate this public safety broadcast into a live map of vessel movements, which quant desks use to watch crude oil tankers approaching refining hubs like Jamnagar, or coal and iron ore vessels calling at major ports such as Paradip and Visakhapatnam, well before customs or company disclosures confirm the volumes. This is one of the cleaner alternative data categories from a compliance standpoint, since AIS is a public safety broadcast by design, not a leaked internal record.

body.title: Stylized example: one refiner's crude sourcing mix inferred from tracked tanker arrivals in a quarter

The actual sourcing mix for any Indian refiner shifts with global crude pricing and sanctions dynamics, which is precisely the kind of shift AIS tracking lets you observe in near real time rather than waiting for a quarterly disclosure.
Geolocation and Foot Traffic: Retail's Physical Pulse

Location panels built from opted-in mobile apps can estimate footfall trends at malls and large-format stores, giving retail-focused strategies an early read on physical demand for chains such as Trent's Westside and Zudio formats, Shoppers Stop, or D-Mart, ahead of quarterly same-store-sales disclosures. Unlike a satellite image, this data starts life close to an individual person's device, which changes its risk profile completely.

body.title: Privacy and airspace rules you cannot skip

children.text: Geolocation panels are only usable responsibly when the data reaches you already aggregated and anonymized, with individual device identifiers stripped out and small-count locations suppressed so no single person's movement can be reconstructed. Buying or building anything closer to individual-level tracking runs directly into the same natural-person test from the previous lesson and brings India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, squarely into play.

If your desk ever considers commissioning custom aerial imagery rather than licensing existing satellite data, remember that drone flights in India are governed by the Drone Rules, 2021, which require registration and restrict flights near airports, borders, and other sensitive zones. This is a real operational constraint, not a formality, and it is a large part of why most desks license existing satellite and aerial imagery rather than flying their own drones over a competitor's plant.

body.title: Applying the Six-Dimension Framework to a Monsoon Play
body.scenario: Your desk is building a strategy around fertilizer and tractor stocks that depends on an early read on monsoon quality across key agricultural states. Two options are on the table: license a commercial NDVI-based crop health feed with three years of history and monthly updates, or build an in-house SAR-based flood and soil moisture pipeline from freely available Sentinel data, with no existing history and a multi-month engineering effort.
body.prompt: Using the six-dimension framework from Chapter 1 (timeliness, breadth, historical depth, signal-to-noise, cost, compliance), how would you weigh these two options for a strategy that rebalances monthly and needs at least five years of backtestable history to be approved by your risk committee?
body.modelAnswer: The historical depth requirement is the deciding factor here. The strategy needs at least five years of backtestable history, and the commercial NDVI feed offers only three years, which on its own may already disqualify it unless it can be extended by reprocessing older Sentinel or Landsat archives. The in-house SAR pipeline has no existing history at all, but Sentinel data itself has been publicly available for years, so a well-built pipeline could, in principle, be backfilled by reprocessing that archive, at the cost of significant engineering time. On timeliness and directness both options are reasonably strong for a monthly rebalance, since neither needs intraday freshness. On cost, the commercial feed is cheaper up front but caps out at its vendor's history, while the in-house build costs more in engineering time but gives full control over backfill depth. On compliance, both are clean, since satellite-derived crop and soil data does not touch personal information. Given the hard five-year history requirement, the correct move is to investigate whether either option can be backfilled from open satellite archives before committing budget, rather than assuming the commercial feed's three years is a fixed limit or that building in-house guarantees a longer history by default.

body.text: Satellite and geolocation data earns its reputation honestly for physical, observable activity: stockpiles, ship movements, crop health, footfall. It cannot see a balance sheet, a management decision, or an accounting choice. Treat it as a demand and activity signal, not a substitute for the fundamental and governance work covered elsewhere in this program.

Companies and locations named in this lesson illustrate concepts only. The AIS sourcing chart is a hypothetical example, not a reported figure. Nothing here is a recommendation to trade any security, and any geolocation or drone-based data project should be reviewed by legal and compliance before it starts.

points: Satellite and geolocation data splits into optical imagery, SAR (radar) imagery, and geolocation or foot traffic panels, each suited to different problems
India's June to September monsoon makes SAR essential for continuous monitoring, since optical satellites lose visibility over much of the country during the cloudiest months

NDVI, calculated as (NIR minus Red) divided by (NIR plus Red), gives an early read on crop health that ripples into tractor, two-wheeler, fertilizer, and rural FMCG demand well before official agricultural data
AIS vessel tracking is a public safety broadcast that vendors aggregate into shipping data, making it one of the cleaner alternative data categories from a compliance standpoint

Geolocation and foot traffic panels must arrive aggregated and anonymized to be used responsibly, since anything closer to individual tracking triggers India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
Custom aerial data collection in India must respect the Drone Rules, 2021, which is a major reason most desks license existing satellite data rather than flying their own imagery missions

None of these sources can see a balance sheet or a management decision, they measure physical activity, and should be combined with fundamental and governance analysis, not used as a replacement for it
